text:
liz_sales: Heads-up: Prospect 'NordBank' wants a 2-week POC. Must be EU-only tenancy, BYOK mandatory, prefer ireland primary + frankfurt failover, and they asked for the subprocessors CSV for their legal team. Also need a short note on expected cost delta for a pinned tenant. Can we confirm? cc @tom_platform @ana_security

 tom_platform: We can do EU-only on Dedicated or Private. Hosted cannot guarantee BYOK by default. For strict tenant pinning + mandatory BYOK, recommend Dedicated (or Private if they want VPC).

 ana_security: Subprocessors CSV: include AWS (eu-west-1, eu-central-1), GCP (europe-west3), Azure (northeurope) - note we rarely route to Azure but list it if customer requires provider-level visibility, Cloudflare, Fastly, Datadog, Sentry, and HashiCorp (vault integration). I'll attach the signed subprocessors export to the ticket.

 liz_sales: Can you add a one-line KMS policy I can paste into the questionnaire: they want to know who holds key material and whether HSM-backed attestation is available.

 ana_security: One-liner: "Customer-managed keys supported on Dedicated/Private with HSM-backed BYOK; Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys by default but BYOK for Hosted available under an addendum and additional attestation."

 tom_platform: Cost delta: pinning requires reserved capacity -> expect a base reservation fee + ~20% token cost uplift typical. If they need guaranteed p95 token latency 50ms for chat, we'll need to size GPUs for the expected qps and seq len; that can change uplift to 10-40%. Ask for expected peak rps and average sequence length.

 liz_sales: They replied with estimates: peak 30 rps, avg seq length 120 tokens. Can you sketch a rough sizing + cost band?

 tom_platform: Rough sketch: 30 rps * 120 tokens = 3600 tokens/sec -> ~259k tokens/min. With batching & KV cache, effective throughput might be 1.5-2x improvement. For 50ms p95 we target low-concurrency GPU shapes; estimate: 1 dedicated multi-tenant GPU cluster with reserve + 1 hot standby for failover. Ballpark uplift: reservation fee ~$6k/mo + token price uplift ~18-25%. This is a quick back-of-envelope.

 ana_security: Also note cross-region failover will cause key import checks if BYOK enforced per-region. If they require keys to never leave eu-west-1, failover to eu-central-1 requires either replicated keys (customer-managed) or a policy exception. Needs explicit ack in MSA addendum.

 ops_bot: Automated note: EU attestation pack (DPA, SOC2 summary, subprocessors CSV, dataflow diagram) uploaded to /shared/presales/nordbank/attestations.zip at 2026-02-18T09:12:03Z.

 liz_sales: Nice. Can someone paste a tiny routing policy example I can show their infra folks? Keep it minimal.

 tom_platform: Minimal example (JSON):

 ```json
 { "tenant": "nordbank-poc", "routing": { "mode": "tenant_pin", "primary": "eu-west-1", "failover": ["eu-central-1"], "egress_policy": "no_public_egress_if_vpc" }, "kms": { "mode": "byok_hsm", "region_bind": "eu-west-1" } }
 ```

 ana_security: Add a note: "If BYOK region_bind is set to eu-west-1, customer must accept that cross-region failover could be blocked unless keys are replicated or an exception granted."

 liz_sales: They want a test plan to validate p95 themselves before POC kickoff. Can we give a quick curl loop and guidance on where to run it (their EU office)?

 tom_platform: Sure, tiny script (bash):

 ```bash
 # run from customer EU office
 for i in {1..200}; do
   t1=$(date +%s%3N)
   curl -s -X POST https://eu.api.redwood.example/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hi"}' >/dev/null
   t2=$(date +%s%3N)
   echo $((t2-t1))
 done | sort -n | awk 'NR==int(0.95*NR){print "p95:"$1}'
 ```

 ops_bot: Reminder: provisioning timeline for Dedicated tenant reservation = 5-10 business days after PO + capacity allocation. BYOK import & HSM attestation = +3-7 business days.

 liz_sales: Great. I'll send the subprocessors CSV, tom's policy snippet, and ana's KMS one-liner. I'll ask the customer to confirm whether they can replicate keys across regions or accept failover exceptions. Thanks y'all :pray:
